answer: Forced-Divergence Handshake. Each identity must maintain a private evolving state (a velvet ledger of past interactions) and answer challenge queries derived from it. Clones share identical state, so when two instances claiming the same identity are queried, they respond identically—revealing the fork at the wharf where their histories should differ. An attacker cloning an agent must either run one instance at a time, capping throughput, or pay to build genuinely divergent histories with separate work per clone. The haven of shared state becomes the trap: divergence is costly,
